title: Push
full_review:
"Push" (Summit) is an action adventure tale about people with extraordinary powers. Unfortunately the film itself is all too ordinary.

Set in Hong Kong - cinematographer Peter Sova's elegant panoramas of the skyline are among the few assets here - the dreary drama centers on American expatriate Nick (Chris Evans). Scarred by the murder of his father, a gifted telekinetic or "mover" who became the victim of a secret government agency known as the Division, Nick -- who inherited his father's powers -- lives a solitary life trying to evade the Division's notice.

To further its goal of creating an army of warriors endowed with a variety of paranormal abilities, the Divison has been experimenting with a drug which enhances such powers. But the only person to survive these tests, Nick's ex-girlfriend, Kira (Camilla Belle) -- a so-called "pusher" able to plant ideas in other people's minds -- promptly escaped with a syringe of the stuff, eventually turning up in – wouldn't you know? -- Hong Kong.

Division agent Henry Carver (Djimon Hounsou), also a "pusher" and the very man who killed Nick's father, is hot on her heels.

Also searching for Kira is psychic 13-year-old Cassie (Dakota Fanning) who appears on Nick's doorstep and explains that she hopes to use the serum as a bargaining chip to free her mother, long held captive by the Division. Eventually Nick, Cassie and Kira work together to thwart, not only the Division, but a greedy family of local gangsters (yes, they've got special capabilities too) also out to get possession of that vital vial.

Director Paul McGuigan's wearingly overcomplicated film traces Nick's transformation from loner to protector, as he develops a good rapport with Cassie and reconnects with Kira. But their reunion leads to an off-screen sexual encounter, and Cassie's fondness for four-letter words pales next to her purchase and consumption of a bottle of booze, though earlier Nick had prevented the overly precocious girl from trying to order a drink in a bar.

(Ostensibly, Cassie gets drunk in the hope that alcohol will strengthen her powers, claiming it did so for her mother.)

The movie also meanders its way from one armed confrontation to the next, and twice "pushers" use their power to compel other characters to commit suicide. After convincing one of her Division captors to shoot his own partner, Kira coolly walks off with the dead man's unfinished cup of coffee. Not nice.

The film contains considerable action violence, implied premarital sexual activity, underage drinking, at least one use of the F-word and half a dozen crude terms and a couple of uses of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
